subject: subjunc vs. subread-align for use with featureCounts

messages.author: 0ebb124842957335
messages.subject: subjunc vs. subread-align for use with featureCounts
parts:
The Subread manual states that subread-align is good enough to generate alignments for use with featureCounts.

I am processing RNA seq. data to analyze both gene expression (at the gene and not the exon level) and sequence variations. I have used subjunc for the latter purpose and I want to know if the alignment files can be used for featureCounts (for gene-level summarization), or if I should align the reads again using subread-align for use with featureCounts.

Thanks.

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: subjunc vs. subread-align for use with featureCounts
parts:
You can use the subjunc alignment results for featureCounts. Subjunc is more stringent in read mapping so as to reduce the false positives in junction calling. However I wouldn't expect much difference in calling differentially expressed genes between using subread-align results and using subjunc results.

Best wishes,
Wei
